text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.
-An opinion poll shows that 44 percent of Norwegians think the government should cancel plans to build natural gas power plants.
-First-quarter results in Norwegian forestry group Norske Skog fell considerably compared to the same year-ago period because of price reductions on its main product.
-Norway's first Jewish museum openes today in the world's northernmost synagogue in Tromsoe.

-The Oslo taxman has confiscated property belonging to Kvaerner chief executive officer Erik Tonseth on grounds he owes the state 5.1 million crowns in taxback payments. Tonseth says he has already paid the money.
-Norwegian natural gas exporters could lose several billion crowns as a consequence of new European energy laws.
-Norway's Norsk Hydro is considering spinning off its fish farming division Hydro Seafood from the company and list it on the Oslo Stock Exchange.
